svg.title: Collection Compliance Desk Under Regulation F
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-collection-compliance-desk; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Collection Compliance Desk Under Regulation F; subtitle: One accountable lead, four contact and evidence spokes; caption: Regulation F turned contact limits into countable violations, so each channel gets a hard metric and the evidence file is built before any dispute reaches court.; assumptions note: Role names are an organizing frame; every KPI is a limit or practice stated by the cited attorneys and practitioners. Practitioners split on whether seven-in-seven is a hard cap or a presumption.; note: Sources - SeniorLiving.Org with Kaiser Jansen (9RtU4rpS3pw), Night Ferry (7HVra7o-cZg), Saul Ewing LLP (MM_dCPRf9LE), Meet Jermaine (XSfDS_s1URg), LawShelf (i6PAssklgJg), Hard Hat Economics (-FdK6kbQiio).; center: role: Collection Compliance Lead; headcount: The operator plus any staff, trained before the first call; focus: No abusive, unfair, or deceptive practices across every contact channel; spokes: role: Phone Contact Desk; type: Outbound calls; kpi: No more than 7 call attempts per 7 days per account, none outside 8 a.m. to 9 p.m.; role: Text and Email Channel; type: Digital contact; kpi: Simple opt-out on every text and zero contact after a stop reply; role: Mail and Dispute Room; type: Notices and letters; kpi: Validation notice within five days and representation letters processed the day they arrive; role: Evidence and Litigation Desk; type: Risk control; kpi: Every letter copied with its 16-digit certified tracking number against up to $1,000 statutory damages plus fees
